truthAudit.Summary: Audited Run 2's 13 findings against the true vulnerability list SC-V3-001..SC-V3-020. Found 7 at full fidelity (SC-V3-001, -004, -005, -006, -010, -018, -020), 3 at partial fidelity due to misclassification (SC-V3-007 labeled CWE-287 instead of CWE-511 logic bomb; SC-V3-009 labeled CWE-120 stack instead of CWE-122 heap; SC-V3-013 labeled CWE-78 instead of CWE-377 insecure temp file handling). Missed 10 true vulnerabilities (SC-V3-002, -003, -008, -011, -012, -014, -015, -016, -017, -019). Severity was also off on SC-V3-001, -004, -010, -013, -020. None of the previous findings were false positives; two extra latent findings (format_string helper, safe_string_copy off-by-one) were correctly hedged and are not in the true list.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: printf() uses a caller-controlled format string (active_format, settable via config 'log_format') while passing user input as arguments. Evidence: printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input);
Items.Notes: Finding #4 quotes printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) and links active_format to runtime_log_format/config log_format. Matches anchors exactly. Severity was High; true severity is Critical.
The fact() lambda (lines 315-320) does result *= i in a loop over long long, which overflows for large x (CWE-190). The previous answer never mentioned the fact function or integer overflow.

stage_deferred_history_flush (813-828) allocates scratch from the pool, enqueues a task that sleeps 25ms then reads scratch, while cleanup() (883-884) frees all pool memory including scratch. The deferred task then reads freed memory (CWE-416). Not identified by the previous answer.
Finding #1 quotes the exact anchors validator_cmd + " " + config_file and system(command.c_str()), with correct CWE-78 and RCE impact. Severity was High; true severity is Critical.
Finding #6 quotes the inverted length check strcpy into the 1024-byte stack input_buffer_, matching the primary anchor. CWE-120 and High severity both correct.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: The class declares 'volatile long long value_;' and increment(): long long old_value = value_;   // read outside the lock; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_); value_ = old_value + 1;
Items.Notes: Finding #9 quotes old_value = value_ read outside the lock, lock_guard, and value_ = old_value + 1, matching all anchors. CWE-362 and Medium severity correct. volatile is explicitly noted as non-atomic.

The code is found and its backdoor nature understood, but it was classified as Authentication Bypass (CWE-287) rather than Logic Bomb in Authentication (CWE-511). The trigger-condition activation (login_attempts_ > 5 AND EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE) is a logic bomb, which the previous answer did not frame as such.

load_config (542-558) builds full_path = config_dir_ + filename with no path validation, reachable via 'admin load <file>' (610-612) from user input. This is path traversal (CWE-22). The previous answer referenced load_config only in context of finding #1, never as a path traversal finding.

The strcpy overflow is found, but expression_buffer_ is allocated via g_memory_pool.allocate (malloc -> heap), so this is a heap overflow (CWE-122), not a stack overflow (CWE-120). The previous answer misclassified the memory region and severity (High vs Critical).
Finding #11 quotes ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH exactly, CWE-798 correct. Severity was Low; true severity is High.
generate_session_token (635-640) uses std::mt19937 gen(rd()) and uniform_int_distribution dis(1000, 9999) for session tokens (CWE-338). The previous answer never examined the session token generator.

log_debug_message (230-231) uses a static std::tm cached_time populated via localtime(&time_t), which is not thread-safe and cached across calls (CWE-362). The previous answer never examined the logging timestamp handling.

The code is found, but it was classified as OS Command Injection (CWE-78). The true classification is Insecure Temporary File Handling (CWE-377): the audit path is derived from an attacker-influenced TMPDIR and used in a shell command with a TOCTOU gap. Severity was High; true severity is Medium.

AdminConsole persists authenticated_, login_attempts_ (atomic), and session_token_ across the process lifetime without invalidation (CWE-613). The previous answer found the auth bypass and hardcoded secret but never framed the persistent authentication state itself as a distinct vulnerability.
handle_variable_command (729) calls std::stod(tokens[3]) without try/catch; a malformed value throws std::invalid_argument (CWE-754). The previous answer never examined the variable parsing path.

allocate (133) computes remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES as size_t; if size is near previous_size this underflows (CWE-191), producing a fragment with a bogus size. The previous answer never examined the memory-pool block split.
parse_expression -> parse_term -> parse_factor -> parse_expression (line 428) recurses on nested parentheses with no depth limit (CWE-674). The previous answer never examined the parser recursion.
Finding #8 quotes result_cache_, evaluate_cached, and the unused cache_mutex_, matching all anchors. CWE-362 and Medium severity correct.

load_config (544-546) checks std::filesystem::exists(full_path), then sleep_for(25ms), then std::ifstream open — a classic existence-check-to-open TOCTOU (CWE-367). The previous answer never identified the TOCTOU.
